item.content:encoded:
Young people across Central Asia are increasingly playing an important role in strengthening communities, promoting social development and addressing emerging security challenges. However, youth can also face vulnerabilities that may expose them to organized crime, drug trafficking, online criminal activities, financial crime and other forms of exploitation.

To address these challenges, the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) is inviting young people from Central Asia to participate in the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026: “Preventing Youth Engagement in Criminal Activities.” This regional workshop will take place from 5 to 9 October 2026 in Issyk-Kul, Kyrgyzstan, bringing together up to 25 young participants for five days of dialogue, interactive learning, networking and youth-led project development.

The forum is designed for young people who are interested in building safer and more resilient communities and who want to contribute to preventing youth involvement in criminal activities across the Central Asian region.

Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026 Overview

The Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum is a regional youth-focused initiative organized by the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) through the Office of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities.

The programme will provide selected participants with an opportunity to examine some of the major crime and security challenges affecting young people and communities across Central Asia.

Participants will not only learn about existing crime-prevention approaches but will also work collaboratively to develop practical, youth-led solutions. An important component of the programme will involve developing project ideas and pitching them to international organizations and donors that support youth-led initiatives.

The forum will therefore combine knowledge development, regional dialogue, practical project development, networking and community engagement.

Event Details

  • Opportunity: Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026
  • Theme: Preventing Youth Engagement in Criminal Activities
  • Organized by: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)
  • Organizing office: Office of the Co-ordinator of OSCE Economic and Environmental Activities
  • Opportunity field: Youth
  • Dates: 5–9 October 2026
  • Location: Issyk-Kul, Kyrgyzstan
  • Number of participants: Up to 25 young people
  • Participation: In person
  • Participation fee: No registration or participation fee
  • Travel support: Covered for selected participants
  • Accommodation: Covered for selected participants
  • Meals: Covered for selected participants
  • Training materials: Covered for selected participants
  • Application deadline: 26 August 2026 at 17:00 CEST

What Is the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum About?

The forum focuses on the prevention of youth engagement in criminal activities and seeks to strengthen young people’s understanding of emerging security and social challenges in Central Asia.

Young people can be particularly vulnerable to criminal recruitment and exploitation. Factors such as unemployment, social exclusion, lack of educational opportunities, online manipulation and economic vulnerability can create conditions that criminal groups may exploit.

The OSCE forum will create a space where young people from Central Asian countries can examine these challenges from a regional perspective and identify approaches that can help communities become more resilient.

Rather than simply providing theoretical training, the programme will encourage participants to think about practical solutions that young people can implement in their own communities.

Key Topics Covered During the Forum

Participants will take part in interactive learning sessions covering several areas related to crime prevention and youth engagement.

1. Organized Crime Recruitment

Participants will explore how organized criminal groups recruit and exploit young people and examine the factors that can make youth vulnerable to criminal involvement.

Understanding recruitment patterns can help young leaders, educators, community organizations and policymakers develop more effective prevention strategies.

2. Drug Trafficking

Drug trafficking is an important regional security concern, and young people can be affected both as potential victims of criminal exploitation and as members of communities experiencing the consequences of drug-related crime.

The forum will provide participants with an opportunity to better understand the challenges associated with drug trafficking and consider approaches to prevention.

3. Financial Crime and Money Laundering

The programme will also address financial crime and money laundering.

Participants can expect to explore how illicit financial activities operate and why financial integrity and awareness are important components of preventing and combating criminal activities.

This knowledge can be particularly valuable for young people interested in governance, economics, law, finance, development and public policy.

4. Online Risks and Social Media

Digital platforms have created new opportunities for communication and education, but they have also introduced new risks.

The forum will examine online risks and the role of social media in relation to youth vulnerability and criminal activities.

Participants will have an opportunity to consider how digital literacy, responsible online engagement and community awareness can contribute to preventing young people from becoming victims or participants in criminal activities.

5. Gender Dimensions of Crime Prevention

The forum will also examine the gender dimensions associated with crime and prevention.

Understanding how criminal activities and vulnerabilities can affect different groups differently is important for developing inclusive and effective prevention initiatives.

6. Evidence-Based Prevention Approaches

Participants will learn about approaches to preventing youth engagement in criminal activities that are informed by evidence and practical experience.

This can help young leaders move beyond general awareness campaigns and develop initiatives based on identified needs, evidence and measurable outcomes.

7. Project Development and Pitching

A practical component of the programme will focus on project development.

Participants will work with their peers to develop youth-led initiatives designed to strengthen community resilience against crime.

They will also have an opportunity to pitch their project ideas to international organizations and donors supporting youth-led solutions.

This element can help participants develop important skills in:

  • Identifying community problems
  • Developing project concepts
  • Designing youth-led interventions
  • Working collaboratively
  • Presenting ideas
  • Communicating project impact
  • Engaging potential partners
  • Pitching projects to donors and international organizations

Why Participate in the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum?

The OSCE forum offers participants several opportunities for personal, professional and community development.

Build Knowledge and Expertise

Participants will gain exposure to a range of issues connected to youth crime prevention, organized crime, drug trafficking, financial crime, online risks and community resilience.

The interactive nature of the sessions is designed to help participants engage with these topics rather than simply receive information through lectures.

Develop Youth-Led Solutions

One of the most practical benefits of the programme is the opportunity to work with other young people to develop innovative initiatives.

Participants can use their understanding of local and regional challenges to develop projects that seek to prevent youth involvement in criminal activities and strengthen community resilience.

Pitch Ideas to International Organizations and Donors

Participants will have the opportunity to present their project ideas to international organizations and donors supporting youth-led solutions.

This can provide valuable exposure to how development and community projects are communicated to potential supporters.

It can also help participants strengthen their project-pitching and advocacy skills.

Expand Your Regional Network

The forum will bring together young people from across Central Asia, creating an opportunity to establish connections with peers who share an interest in youth development, community engagement, security and crime prevention.

Participants can potentially build relationships with:

  • Young leaders
  • Youth activists
  • Community representatives
  • Practitioners
  • Experts
  • International organizations
  • Other stakeholders working on crime prevention and youth development

Regional networks can be valuable for future collaborations, youth initiatives and community projects.

Participate Without Paying a Registration Fee

Selected participants will not be required to pay a registration or participation fee.

This makes the programme accessible to eligible young people who may otherwise face financial barriers to participating in an international regional event.

What Costs Does the OSCE Cover?

For selected participants, the OSCE will provide comprehensive participation support.

The programme covers:

  • Travel
  • Accommodation
  • Meals
  • Training materials

Participants therefore do not need to pay a registration or participation fee to attend the forum.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the official application information for any additional logistical instructions concerning travel and participation.

Who Can Apply for the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum?

The opportunity is specifically intended for young people from the five Central Asian countries represented in the programme.

Applicants must meet all of the core eligibility requirements established by the organizers.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be 18 to 25 years old by 4 October 2026.

This means applicants must fall within the specified age range immediately before the forum begins.

Citizenship Requirement

Applicants must be citizens of one of the following countries:

  1. Kazakhstan
  2. Kyrgyzstan
  3. Tajikistan
  4. Turkmenistan
  5. Uzbekistan

The programme is therefore specifically targeted at young people from Central Asia rather than applicants from other regions of the world.

English Language Requirement

Applicants must be fluent in English.

This is an important requirement because no interpretation will be provided during the forum.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable participating in discussions, interactive sessions, group activities and project presentations in English.

Relevant Experience or Interest

Applicants should have experience or a strong interest in one or more relevant areas, including:

  • Youth crime prevention
  • Community engagement
  • Rule of law
  • Financial integrity
  • Education
  • Social development
  • Related fields

Applicants do not necessarily need to be established professionals in these areas. The opportunity also welcomes young people with a strong interest in relevant issues.

Community Engagement

Applicants should be active in their communities and demonstrate an interest in regional youth cooperation.

This means applicants should ideally be able to demonstrate how they contribute to or engage with their communities and why regional cooperation among young people is important to them.

Availability to Attend in Person

Selected participants must be available to attend the full event in person from 5 to 9 October 2026 in Issyk-Kul, Kyrgyzstan.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they can commit to the entire programme before applying.

What Kind of Applicants Would Be a Strong Fit?

Although meeting the eligibility requirements is essential, applicants may strengthen their applications by clearly demonstrating their interest and involvement in relevant areas.

A strong applicant could be someone who:

  • Has participated in youth-led community initiatives.
  • Works or volunteers in youth development.
  • Has experience with community engagement.
  • Is interested in crime prevention or public safety.
  • Has an interest in the rule of law.
  • Works in education or social development.
  • Has an interest in financial integrity or combating financial crime.
  • Has experience organizing youth activities.
  • Has participated in regional youth programmes.
  • Wants to develop a community-based solution to a crime-related challenge.
  • Is interested in developing projects for young people.
  • Can collaborate effectively with participants from other Central Asian countries.
  • Is comfortable communicating and presenting ideas in English.

Applicants should focus on demonstrating genuine engagement rather than simply listing broad interests.

How to Apply for the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026

Eligible applicants interested in participating should submit their application through the application platform provided by the organizers.

A Google account sign-in is required to access the application.

When preparing the application, applicants should make sure that the information they provide clearly demonstrates their eligibility, community involvement and interest in preventing youth engagement in criminal activities.

It is particularly important to explain relevant experience or interests in areas such as youth development, community engagement, education, social development, rule of law, financial integrity or crime prevention.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

26 August 2026 at 17:00 CEST

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Technical problems, incomplete information or difficulties accessing the application form could prevent a submission before the deadline.

Applicants should also take into account the time difference between Central Asia and Central European Summer Time when planning their submission.

Important Application Tips

1. Demonstrate Your Community Involvement

Do not simply state that you are interested in youth development or crime prevention.

Where possible, explain how you have participated in community activities, youth initiatives, education programmes, volunteer work or other relevant activities.

2. Connect Your Experience to the Forum

Show why the forum is relevant to your interests and previous activities.

For example, if you have worked on youth engagement, explain how learning about crime prevention could help you strengthen your future community initiatives.

3. Highlight Your Regional Perspective

The forum is designed as a regional dialogue, so applicants should demonstrate an interest in cooperation with young people from other Central Asian countries.

4. Demonstrate Your Ability to Communicate in English

Because no interpretation will be available, applicants should make sure their application demonstrates their ability to participate effectively in English-language discussions and activities.

5. Think About a Potential Project Idea

The programme includes project development and pitching. Applicants may therefore benefit from thinking about a community challenge they would like to address.

A potential idea could focus on areas such as:

  • Youth awareness
  • Digital safety
  • Community education
  • Youth employment and resilience
  • Prevention of criminal recruitment
  • Financial literacy
  • Social inclusion
  • Youth participation
  • Community-based prevention

The idea does not necessarily need to be fully developed before applying, but having a clear understanding of a problem affecting young people can help applicants participate more effectively.

APPLY HERE

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026 fully funded?

The OSCE will cover travel, accommodation, meals and training materials for selected participants. There is also no registration or participation fee.

Where will the forum take place?

The event will take place in Issyk-Kul, Kyrgyzstan.

When will the forum take place?

The forum is scheduled for 5–9 October 2026.

How many young people will participate?

The OSCE plans to bring together up to 25 young participants.

What is the age requirement?

Applicants must be 18–25 years old by 4 October 2026.

Can applicants from outside Central Asia apply?

No. The opportunity is specifically for citizens of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

Is English required?

Yes. Applicants must be fluent in English because no interpretation will be provided.

Can I attend virtually?

No. Applicants must be available to attend the full programme in person.

Is there an application fee?

No. There is no registration or participation fee.

What is the application deadline?

Applications must be submitted by 26 August 2026 at 17:00 CEST.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026 in Kyrgyzstan.

Final Thoughts

The Central Asia Youth Dialogue Forum 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for young people from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan to strengthen their understanding of crime prevention while contributing to regional dialogue and youth-led solutions.

Through interactive sessions, participants will explore important issues including organized crime recruitment, drug trafficking, financial crime, money laundering, online risks, social media, gender dimensions and evidence-based prevention approaches.

The programme goes beyond classroom learning by giving participants the opportunity to collaborate with peers, develop practical project ideas and pitch youth-led solutions to international organizations and donors. The travel, accommodation, meals and training materials provided by the OSCE also reduce the financial barriers associated with participating in an international regional programme.

For eligible young people who are passionate about community development, youth cooperation, social resilience, rule of law or preventing youth involvement in criminal activities, this forum could provide valuable knowledge, networks and practical project-development experience.

Eligible applicants should submit their applications before 26 August 2026 at 17:00 CEST.

item.content:encoded:
The OECD Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs (ELS) is offering a research-oriented internship for a highly qualified and motivated student with a background in economics or applied social sciences.

The internship is based within the Jobs and Income Division of ELS, the team responsible for important OECD research on labour markets, employment, job quality and working conditions. The role provides an opportunity to work alongside economists on research examining labour shortages and workers’ preferences, while gaining experience in an international policy and research environment.

The internship is particularly suited to students with strong quantitative research, econometric, analytical and writing skills who are interested in applied labour economics and evidence-based policymaking.

Internship Overview

The intern will contribute to a new research project examining why labour shortages persist in certain occupations and sectors and how workers value different characteristics of jobs.

The project uses an original survey incorporating a discrete choice experiment to investigate workers’ preferences regarding different job characteristics.

Depending on the priorities of the team and the candidate’s skills, the intern may also contribute to related OECD research covering:

  • Working time across countries.
  • Job quality.
  • Labour market transitions.
  • Labour shortages.
  • Workers’ preferences.
  • Comparative labour market research.

The internship also provides exposure to the OECD’s wider policy and research environment, including seminars, discussions with experts and opportunities to present work in an international setting.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is open to students who meet the following requirements:

  • Must be a national of an OECD member country.
  • Must be enrolled in a full-time graduate degree programme in economics or a closely related field throughout the entire internship.
  • The position is particularly suited to students at an advanced stage of their studies, including:
    • PhD candidates.
    • Master’s students in the final year of their programme.
  • Must be available for at least four months.
  • Must have an excellent command of English.
  • Must have strong writing, drafting and communication skills.
  • Must possess solid quantitative research abilities.
  • Must have familiarity with statistical or econometric software such as Stata, R or Python.
  • Must be comfortable working in a multicultural and international environment.

APPLY HERE

Additional Skills That Would Be an Advantage

Some skills are not mandatory but would strengthen an application.

These include:

  • Knowledge of German, particularly because the research survey will be conducted in Germany.
  • Experience with survey design.
  • Experience with questionnaire testing.
  • Knowledge of discrete choice experiments.
  • Experience estimating discrete choice models.
  • Previous empirical research experience.
  • Experience working with large or complex datasets.

Knowledge of German is specifically described as a strong advantage but is not mandatory.

What Will the Intern Work On?

The successful candidate will work closely with economists in the ELS Directorate.

Responsibilities may include several stages of the research process.

1. Developing the Survey

The intern may contribute to developing a survey instrument that incorporates a discrete choice experiment.

This can involve:

  • Selecting relevant attributes.
  • Designing the experimental component.
  • Developing the questionnaire.
  • Drafting survey questions.
  • Ensuring that the survey can effectively capture workers’ preferences.

2. Testing the Survey

Before the survey is fully launched, the intern may participate in testing its design.

This can involve:

  • Conducting cognitive interviews.
  • Supporting a soft launch.
  • Reviewing feedback.
  • Identifying problems with the questionnaire.
  • Revising the instrument based on testing results.

This provides practical experience with the process of turning a research concept into a functioning empirical survey.

3. Working With the Survey Company

The intern may also liaise with a professional survey company responsible for elements of the research process.

Tasks can include supporting work related to:

  • Survey scripting.
  • Translation.
  • Sampling.
  • Quality control.
  • Fieldwork monitoring.

This gives the intern exposure to the operational side of large-scale empirical research.

4. Analysing the Data

Once the survey data have been collected, the intern may contribute to quantitative analysis.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Analysing survey data.
  • Constructing tables.
  • Producing figures.
  • Conducting robustness checks.
  • Supporting empirical research and interpretation.

Strong quantitative skills are therefore particularly important for this position.

Technical and Research Skills

This internship is strongly research-oriented, meaning applicants should be comfortable working with quantitative evidence.

Experience with statistical and econometric tools such as:

  • Stata
  • R
  • Python

is expected.

Applicants should also be able to demonstrate their ability to communicate empirical findings clearly through written research.

Previous experience with survey design, discrete choice experiments or empirical labour-market research can further strengthen an application.

Shortlisted Candidates

Applicants who are shortlisted may be asked to participate in an additional technical discussion.

The discussion may focus on:

  • A submitted writing sample.
  • Previous empirical research.
  • Data construction.
  • Methodological decisions.
  • Limitations of the analysis.
  • The applicant’s approach to empirical research.

Shortlisted candidates may also be asked to provide a reference letter from an academic supervisor or previous employer.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to discuss their research work in detail and explain not only what they did, but also why they selected particular methods and what limitations their analysis has.

Internship Duration

The internship has a minimum duration of four months.

It can be extended for up to six months.

The preferred arrangement is a full-time internship of approximately 40 hours per week.

Start Date

The expected start date is:

Mid- to late October 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Location and Working Arrangement

The internship is based at OECD headquarters in Paris, France.

The preferred arrangement is in-person, although partial remote work may be possible.

This provides interns with the opportunity to work directly within an international organisation and interact with economists, researchers and policy professionals from different countries.

Internship Allowance

The OECD provides a monthly allowance of:

EUR 1,000 per month

This financial support is intended to contribute toward the intern’s living expenses during the internship.

Applicants should nevertheless consider the cost of living in Paris when planning for the internship period.

Deadline

Application deadline: Friday, 4 September 2026

Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline and ensure that all required documents are complete.

How to Apply

Applicants are required to submit three main documents.

Visit HERE to learn more  about the OECD Research Internship in Employment, Labour and Social Affairs Apply by 4 September 2026

1. Curriculum Vitae

Submit a CV that clearly presents your:

  • Educational background.
  • Research experience.
  • Quantitative skills.
  • Relevant work experience.
  • Statistical and econometric software skills.
  • Publications or research projects, where applicable.
  • Nationality.

Your nationality must be specified in the CV.

2. Writing Sample

Applicants must provide a recent piece of empirical work written in English.

The writing sample should preferably be sole-authored rather than co-authored, allowing the selection team to assess the applicant’s individual research and writing abilities.

A strong writing sample should demonstrate:

  • Clear research questions.
  • Appropriate methodology.
  • Quantitative analysis.
  • Good data interpretation.
  • Strong academic writing.
  • Awareness of methodological limitations.

3. Cover Letter

Applicants should also submit a short and concise cover letter.

The cover letter should explain why the candidate is interested in the internship and why their academic and research background makes them suitable for the position.

Applications should be sent to:

andrea.garnero@oecd.org

How to Make Your Application Competitive

Because this is a research-focused position, applicants should make sure their application demonstrates more than simply an interest in economics.

A competitive application should clearly show:

  1. Strong quantitative ability
    Highlight your experience with Stata, R, Python or other relevant research tools.
  2. Empirical research experience
    Your writing sample should demonstrate that you can work with real-world data and draw appropriate conclusions.
  3. Strong writing ability
    The OECD specifically requires strong drafting and communication skills.
  4. Knowledge of labour economics or related fields
    Experience studying employment, wages, labour markets, social policy or related topics can be particularly relevant.
  5. Research maturity
    Be prepared to explain your methodological choices and acknowledge limitations in your previous research.
  6. International outlook
    The role involves comparative research across countries, so an interest in international economic and labour-market issues is valuable.
  7. Clear motivation
    Your cover letter should demonstrate why working with the OECD ELS Directorate fits your academic and professional objectives.

Why This OECD Internship Is Valuable

The internship offers more than short-term work experience.

Successful candidates will have the opportunity to participate in research connected to important labour-market policy questions, including why shortages persist in particular occupations and how workers value different job characteristics.

The OECD’s current labour-market research continues to examine structural labour shortages, worker preferences, demographic changes, skills mismatches and changes in working arrangements.

The intern will also gain exposure to:

  • International economic research.
  • Comparative labour-market analysis.
  • Survey research.
  • Econometric analysis.
  • Policy-oriented research.
  • International experts.
  • OECD seminars and discussions.
  • Professional research networks.

Conclusion

The OECD Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs Internship is a strong opportunity for advanced Master’s and PhD students interested in economics, labour markets, applied social science and quantitative research.

The position combines empirical research with real-world policy questions and gives the successful candidate the opportunity to work alongside OECD economists in Paris.

Applicants should particularly focus on demonstrating their quantitative research skills, empirical experience, English writing ability and familiarity with statistical or econometric tools.

The application deadline is 4 September 2026, with the internship expected to begin in mid- to late October 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter.

item.content:encoded:
The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is one of Africa’s most ambitious efforts to create a more integrated and connected continental economy. The agreement is designed to reduce barriers to trade, encourage the movement of goods and services across African borders, and create greater opportunities for businesses, entrepreneurs and consumers.

A major part of achieving this vision is digitalisation. As African economies become increasingly dependent on digital platforms, electronic payments, digital identity and data-driven services, Africa needs the digital infrastructure that allows businesses and people to participate in cross-border trade more easily.

This is where Africa Digital Access and Public Infrastructure for Trade (ADAPT) comes in.

What Is the African Continental Free Trade Area?

The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is a flagship project of the African Union’s Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want. Its central ambition is to create a more integrated African market by reducing barriers that make it difficult and expensive to trade across national borders.

The agreement covers a broad range of economic activities, including:

  • Trade in goods
  • Trade in services
  • Digital trade
  • Investment
  • Trade facilitation
  • Economic integration
  • Cross-border business activity

Rather than African countries operating primarily as separate national markets, AfCFTA seeks to make it easier for businesses to reach customers and partners across the continent.

The long-term objective is to increase intra-African trade, particularly trade involving value-added goods and services produced within Africa.

Why Creating One African Market Matters

Africa has a large and diverse consumer and business market, but trade between African countries can still be complicated by differences in regulations, customs procedures, payment systems, identification systems, logistics and access to information.

These barriers can make cross-border business more expensive and time-consuming, particularly for smaller businesses.

AfCFTA aims to address these challenges by creating a framework for greater economic integration.

The figures provided by the AfCFTA Secretariat illustrate the scale of the project:

  • 54 AU member states had signed the AfCFTA Agreement as of January 2025.
  • 50 State Parties were reported as of February 2026.
  • The initiative has the potential to help lift 30 million people out of extreme poverty.
  • Estimates indicate a potential $450 billion increase in income in Africa by 2035, representing approximately a 7% gain.

These figures demonstrate why AfCFTA is much more than a conventional trade agreement. It represents an attempt to reshape how African economies interact with one another.

APPLY HERE

What Is ADAPT?

Africa Digital Access and Public Infrastructure for Trade (ADAPT) is designed to provide the digital infrastructure needed to help make the AfCFTA vision practical.

The basic idea is straightforward: you cannot build an effective single African market without the digital systems that allow people and businesses to interact across borders.

ADAPT focuses on connecting critical digital components, particularly:

  1. Digital identity
  2. Data infrastructure
  3. Digital payments
  4. Access to digital services
  5. Infrastructure supporting cross-border trade

By bringing these systems together, ADAPT can help reduce some of the practical barriers that businesses face when attempting to operate across African markets.

The Role of Digital Identity

Digital identity can play an important role in cross-border commerce.

Businesses and individuals frequently need to prove who they are when accessing financial services, registering businesses, completing transactions or interacting with government systems.

Interoperable digital identity infrastructure can potentially make these processes more efficient by allowing trusted digital credentials to be used across different systems.

For businesses operating across borders, this could mean:

  • Easier verification
  • More efficient onboarding
  • Reduced administrative processes
  • Greater access to digital financial services
  • Improved trust between businesses and customers

The Importance of Data

Data is another fundamental component of a modern digital economy.

Businesses need reliable information about markets, customers, regulations, prices and trade opportunities. Governments also need data to understand economic activity and design effective policies.

ADAPT’s focus on digital infrastructure can therefore support a more connected data environment for African trade.

Better digital data systems can help create opportunities for:

  • Market intelligence
  • Digital commerce
  • Trade information
  • Business registration
  • Regulatory compliance
  • Economic planning
  • Cross-border services

Digital Payments and Cross-Border Trade

One of the major challenges facing African businesses is the ability to make and receive payments efficiently across borders.

Digital payment infrastructure can help address this challenge by making transactions faster, more accessible and potentially less expensive.

For an entrepreneur selling products to customers in another African country, for example, a reliable digital payment system can reduce the friction involved in completing a transaction.

This is particularly important for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which may not have the resources to navigate complicated international payment systems.

How ADAPT Can Support African Businesses

The success of a continental market ultimately depends on whether businesses can actually use it.

Digital infrastructure can help businesses participate in the African market by making it easier to:

  • Discover customers in other countries
  • Receive digital payments
  • Verify customers and business partners
  • Access market information
  • Complete administrative procedures
  • Provide digital services across borders
  • Participate in e-commerce
  • Expand into new African markets

This could be particularly valuable for entrepreneurs and MSMEs seeking to expand beyond their domestic markets.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AfCFTA and ADAPT: Building a Connected Digital Single Market for Africa

ADAPT and Digital Trade

Digital trade is becoming increasingly important to Africa’s economic future.

Businesses no longer need to physically establish an office in another country to serve customers there. A company can sell products through an online platform, provide professional services remotely, receive digital payments and communicate with customers across borders.

However, this requires supporting infrastructure.

ADAPT can therefore be viewed as part of the digital foundation required for AfCFTA to function effectively in an increasingly digital economy.

Who Can Benefit From a More Connected African Market?

The benefits of a digitally connected African market could extend across several groups, including:

1. Entrepreneurs and MSMEs

Small businesses could gain access to customers and suppliers in markets beyond their home countries.

2. Digital Businesses

Technology companies, e-commerce platforms and fintech businesses could benefit from a larger potential market.

3. Consumers

Consumers could potentially gain access to a wider variety of African products and services.

4. Governments

Governments can benefit from improved digital systems for trade administration, regulation and economic planning.

5. Investors

A more integrated African market can create opportunities for investment in businesses, infrastructure and digital services.

6. Professional Service Providers

Consultants, software developers, designers, financial professionals and other service providers can potentially serve clients across borders through digital platforms.

The Bigger Vision: One African Market

AfCFTA’s ultimate ambition is not simply to increase the number of products traded between African countries.

It is about creating an environment where African businesses can increasingly think of Africa as a market rather than only their individual national economies.

Digital infrastructure is an important part of making this possible.

A trader in Zambia, for example, should increasingly be able to explore opportunities in another African market, communicate with potential customers, verify business information, complete transactions and receive payment without being overwhelmed by unnecessary administrative and technological barriers.

ENQUERIES

Conclusion

The African Continental Free Trade Area provides the framework for greater economic integration across Africa, while initiatives such as ADAPT focus on the digital infrastructure required to support that integration.

Digital identity, data and payments may appear to be separate technologies, but together they form an important foundation for modern cross-border commerce.

As Africa continues to expand its digital economy, building interoperable infrastructure will be essential to ensuring that entrepreneurs, MSMEs, consumers and governments can participate in a genuinely connected continental market.

item.content:encoded:
The DAAD Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines offer high-achieving students from developing and emerging countries an opportunity to pursue a full-time Master’s degree in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering at a university in Germany.

The programme is designed to support talented young academics and future professionals who want to build advanced expertise in innovation-driven STEM fields and use that knowledge to strengthen their academic and professional careers.

Funding can be provided for 10 to 24 months, depending on the standard duration of the selected Master’s programme, with funding beginning in 2027.

About the DAAD STEM Scholarship

The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) provides scholarships to international students and researchers seeking to study or conduct research in Germany.

The Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines specifically target students from developing and emerging countries who have demonstrated strong academic performance and want to pursue a Master’s degree in one of the following areas:

  • Mathematics
  • Computer Science
  • Natural Sciences
  • Engineering

The programme focuses on STEM fields that contribute to innovation, technological development and the future workforce.

Successful applicants can study at a state or state-recognised university in Germany, provided that their chosen programme meets the scholarship requirements.

What the Scholarship Covers

The scholarship provides substantial financial support throughout the funded study period.

Successful scholars receive:

  • €992 per month as a scholarship payment.
  • Payments toward health, accident and personal liability insurance.
  • A travel allowance, subject to the applicable conditions and application.
  • An annual study allowance of €460.

Depending on individual circumstances and eligibility, additional support may also be available.

Additional Benefits

Scholars may be able to apply for:

  • A monthly rent subsidy.
  • A monthly allowance for accompanying family members.
  • Additional financial support related to disability or chronic illness where justified costs are not covered elsewhere.
  • Reimbursement of carbon-offset payments for air travel.
  • Language-learning support.

For scholarship periods longer than six months, DAAD may also provide support for language learning, including:

  • Fees for an online language course.
  • A German language course in Germany before the start of the study programme, where DAAD determines that this is necessary.
  • An allowance for a personally selected German language course during the scholarship period.
  • Reimbursement of fees for TestDaF or DSH examinations under the applicable conditions.

Important: The Master’s Programme Must Be Tuition-Free

One of the most important requirements is that applicants must select a tuition-free Master’s programme.

The DAAD scholarship itself does not cover tuition fees. Therefore, applicants should carefully check the tuition arrangements of their chosen university and degree programme before applying.

The selected programme must also be:

  • Full-time.
  • On-campus.
  • At a state or state-recognised university in Germany.
  • In mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering.
  • Tuition-free.
  • Starting in the winter semester 2027/28.

Interdisciplinary programmes can qualify if they have a clearly designated STEM focus.

Programmes that have already started in Germany cannot receive funding under this scholarship.

Programmes that include integrated study periods outside Germany are also excluded.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is aimed at high-achieving students from developing and emerging countries who intend to pursue a STEM Master’s degree in Germany.

Applicants must have completed a first university degree recognised in Germany, such as a Bachelor’s degree, by the application deadline at the latest.

Applicants who already hold a Master’s degree by the application deadline are not eligible for this particular scholarship programme.

The scholarship is therefore particularly relevant to students who have completed their undergraduate studies and are now looking to advance their education through a STEM Master’s programme in Germany.

APPLY HERE

Eligible Fields of Study

Applicants must choose a qualifying programme within the STEM disciplines.

1. Mathematics

This can include eligible Master’s programmes focused on areas such as mathematics, applied mathematics, statistics and related mathematical disciplines.

2. Computer Science

Relevant programmes may include computer science, information technology, software-related disciplines, artificial intelligence and other qualifying computing fields.

3. Natural Sciences

This category covers qualifying programmes within the natural sciences.

4. Engineering

Applicants may pursue eligible engineering disciplines offered by German universities.

For interdisciplinary programmes, applicants should ensure that the programme has a clearly defined STEM focus.

Duration of the Scholarship

The scholarship can support students for between 10 and 24 months.

The actual duration depends on the standard length of the selected Master’s degree.

For example, if the chosen Master’s programme normally takes two years to complete, the applicant should request the scholarship for the full two-year period in the application.

After the first year, the scholar’s academic performance will be reviewed.

If the academic progress indicates that the student is likely to successfully complete the programme within a reasonable period, funding can continue as planned.

Funding must begin in 2027 and normally starts on 1 October 2027, although it may begin earlier if the scholar is required to complete a German language course before starting the degree.

Selection Process

DAAD states that only applications containing all mandatory documents will be considered.

Incomplete applications can be excluded from the selection process for formal reasons.

The selection process involves several important stages.

1. Application Review and Pre-Selection

Applications are initially assessed based on the submitted documents.

Particular attention is given to:

  • Academic achievements.
  • Previous course of study.
  • Language skills.
  • Relevant internships.
  • Relevant professional experience, where applicable.

Applicants who perform strongly during the initial assessment may be pre-selected.

2. Interview

Pre-selected applicants are invited to an interview with an independent selection committee consisting of university teachers.

The interview may take place either physically or virtually.

The interview is an important part of the selection process because it allows the committee to assess the applicant’s motivation, authenticity, academic plans and personal potential.

Key Selection Criteria

Applicants are assessed across several major areas.

Academic Qualification

The committee considers:

  • Academic performance.
  • Previous studies.
  • Knowledge of the language of instruction or working language.
  • Relevant internships and work experience where applicable.

Strong academic preparation is therefore an important part of a competitive application.

Quality of the Study Project

Applicants must demonstrate that they have carefully considered their proposed study programme.

The committee considers:

  • The quality of the proposed study project.
  • Preparation for the study programme.
  • Knowledge of the selected degree programme.
  • Choice of university.
  • Evidence of preliminary research.
  • Contacts established with the prospective university where applicable.
  • How the proposed Master’s degree fits into the applicant’s broader academic and professional development.

Applicants should therefore avoid selecting a programme without explaining why it is relevant to their long-term goals.

Personal and Professional Potential

The committee also considers the applicant’s potential and motivation.

This includes:

  • Academic motivation.
  • Personal reasons for studying in Germany.
  • German language skills where relevant.
  • Expected academic development.
  • Expected professional development.
  • Personal development.
  • Extracurricular activities.
  • Social commitment.
  • Relevant knowledge and skills.

Applicants should demonstrate not only that they are academically capable, but also that the opportunity will contribute meaningfully to their future plans.

Equal Opportunity Considerations

DAAD also takes equal-opportunity considerations into account during the selection process.

Applicants may provide information about special circumstances that may have affected their educational or professional journey.

Examples include:

  • Disability.
  • Chronic or prolonged illness.
  • Raising children.
  • Caring for relatives.
  • Refugee background.
  • Significant employment responsibilities required to finance studies.

Applicants who have experienced such circumstances can provide relevant information in the application form so that the selection committee can consider their situation appropriately.

When Does Funding Begin?

The scholarship funding must begin in 2027.

The normal starting date is 1 October 2027, although an earlier start may be possible when a German language course is required before the Master’s programme begins.

The scholarship is specifically intended for Master’s programmes beginning in the winter term 2027/28.

Application Deadline

Deadline: The information provided does not state a single universal application deadline.

Applicants should therefore check the official DAAD scholarship database and the specific application information applicable to their country of origin and programme before preparing their submission.

Because application deadlines can be tied to the relevant DAAD call and applicant country, prospective applicants should not assume that one deadline applies to everyone.

Visit HERE to learn about the DAAD Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines 2027/28

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should begin preparing well in advance rather than waiting until the application period is close to closing.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate:

  1. Strong academic performance
    Highlight relevant academic achievements and STEM-related coursework.
  2. A clear study plan
    Explain why the chosen Master’s programme is appropriate for your academic and professional development.
  3. A suitable German university
    Research universities and tuition-free STEM Master’s programmes carefully before applying.
  4. Strong motivation
    Clearly explain why studying in Germany is important for your future.
  5. Relevant experience
    Include internships, employment, research, projects and other experiences relevant to your chosen field.
  6. Language preparation
    Pay attention to the language requirements of the selected programme and demonstrate the required language skills.
  7. Complete documentation
    Make sure every mandatory document is submitted because incomplete applications can be excluded from consideration.

Why This Opportunity Matters

The DAAD STEM scholarship can provide international students with an opportunity to gain advanced academic qualifications in one of Europe’s major centres for science, technology and innovation.

For students from developing and emerging countries, completing a STEM Master’s degree in Germany can provide access to advanced academic environments, international networks and professional development opportunities.

The scholarship is particularly valuable because it combines a monthly financial allowance with additional support for insurance, travel and study-related expenses, subject to the programme’s conditions.

Conclusion

The DAAD Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines provide an important opportunity for talented students from developing and emerging countries to pursue a tuition-free Master’s degree in Germany in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering.

With funding of €992 per month, insurance support, a study allowance, travel assistance and potential additional benefits, the programme can significantly reduce the financial burden associated with studying abroad.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. They must have completed a recognised first degree by the relevant deadline, must not already hold a Master’s degree, and must choose an eligible tuition-free STEM Master’s programme beginning in the 2027/28 winter term.

Prospective applicants should begin researching eligible German universities and programmes early and consult the official DAAD scholarship database for the exact application deadline and country-specific requirements.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 2027 Whitley Awards, a prestigious conservation funding opportunity supporting grassroots conservation leaders who are developing practical, science-based solutions to protect biodiversity, strengthen communities, and create lasting environmental impact.

Awarded annually, the Whitley Awards provide financial support and international recognition to conservationists who are already leading vital projects and need additional resources to scale up proven approaches.

For 2027, each Whitley Award provides £50,000 in project funding for one year, alongside international profile-raising opportunities, communications and media support, peer learning, training, and collaboration opportunities.

The application deadline is 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026.

Whitley Awards 2027: Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: 2027 Whitley Awards
  • Funding: £50,000 per award
  • Funding period: One year
  • Focus: Grassroots conservation and biodiversity
  • Target applicants: Dynamic, mid-career conservationists leading proven conservation projects
  • Geographic focus: International, with winners being nationals of the countries where they work
  • Application method: Online application
  • Nomination required: No
  • Referees required: Three
  • Application deadline: 23:59 GMT, Friday, 30 October 2026
  • Award ceremony: London, Spring 2027
  • Additional opportunities: International recognition, communications and media support, peer learning, training, collaboration, and eligibility for future Continuation Funding and the Whitley Gold Award

What Are the Whitley Awards?

The Whitley Awards are annual conservation awards that recognise grassroots conservation leaders working to address biodiversity challenges through practical, science-based solutions.

The awards are designed to support conservationists who are already implementing projects with demonstrated potential and who need additional funding to expand or strengthen their impact.

The Whitley Awards place considerable importance on solutions that are:

  • Rooted in science;
  • Embedded within local communities;
  • Focused on practical conservation action;
  • Designed to deliver lasting impact;
  • Connected to local knowledge and community engagement; and
  • Capable of being scaled up with additional support.

The programme’s emphasis on grassroots conservation means that the awards are not simply intended to fund theoretical research or projects that exist only at the planning stage. Applicants are expected to demonstrate proven work and explain how additional funding can help them take their conservation efforts to the next level.

£50,000 Conservation Funding for One Year

Each successful Whitley Award provides £50,000 in project funding over one year.

This funding can provide conservation leaders with the resources needed to strengthen existing initiatives, expand successful interventions, increase community participation, and generate greater conservation impact.

For conservation projects that have already demonstrated results but require additional resources to scale, the award can represent a significant opportunity to move from successful local implementation toward broader and more sustainable impact.

Who Should Apply for the Whitley Awards?

The Whitley Awards are intended for dynamic, mid-career conservationists who are leading vital conservation projects.

The programme is particularly suited to conservation leaders who have already established practical work and are seeking additional resources to scale up their impact.

According to the eligibility information provided, applicants should be:

  • Leading an established conservation project;
  • Working on practical conservation action;
  • Using approaches founded on science;
  • Working closely with grassroots communities;
  • Seeking to scale up proven work;
  • Nationals of the country in which they are working; and
  • Able to demonstrate that their project would benefit from additional funding, greater visibility, and international support.

Importantly, applicants do not need to be invited or nominated to apply for a Whitley Award.

What Does “Proven Work” Mean?

A central aspect of the Whitley Awards is the emphasis on proven conservation work.

The programme is looking for conservation leaders who have moved beyond simply identifying a problem and proposing a possible solution.

Applicants should instead be able to demonstrate that their conservation approach is already being implemented and has generated evidence, experience, results, or other indications that it works.

The award is then intended to help these leaders scale up or strengthen that existing work.

This makes the Whitley Awards particularly relevant to conservationists who can demonstrate:

  • An established project;
  • Practical field experience;
  • Evidence of conservation results;
  • Community involvement;
  • A science-based methodology;
  • A clear need for additional funding; and
  • A realistic plan for expanding their impact.

Grassroots Community Engagement Is Essential

Community involvement is an important component of the Whitley Awards.

Eligible projects must involve communities at the grassroots level and deliver practical action founded on science.

This means that applicants should be able to demonstrate how local communities participate in or benefit from the conservation project.

Projects should not simply impose externally developed conservation interventions on communities. The Whitley Awards emphasise solutions rooted in local knowledge, community engagement, and long-term commitment.

Applicants should therefore clearly explain:

  1. Which communities are involved.
  2. How those communities participate in the project.
  3. What challenges communities face.
  4. How the conservation intervention addresses those challenges.
  5. What benefits communities receive.
  6. How local knowledge informs the project.
  7. How the project will maintain long-term community engagement.

Science-Based Conservation Action

Another important requirement is that projects deliver practical conservation action that is founded on science.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to explain the scientific basis of their conservation approach.

This could include evidence, research, monitoring, data, ecological knowledge, established conservation methods, or other scientifically informed approaches that underpin the project.

The objective is to support conservation interventions that are both practical and credible, rather than initiatives that lack an evidence base.

What Conservation Challenges Can the Awards Address?

The information supplied does not provide an exhaustive list of conservation themes or species that are eligible for funding.

However, the Whitley Awards broadly focus on conservation leaders working to address the biodiversity crisis through solutions based on local knowledge, community engagement, science, and long-term commitment.

This means the opportunity can be relevant to conservation initiatives addressing different biodiversity and environmental challenges, provided that the project meets the Whitley Fund for Nature’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants should consult the official eligibility criteria before assuming that a particular conservation theme or activity qualifies for funding.

Why Apply for a Whitley Award?

The financial grant is only one component of the opportunity.

Winning a Whitley Award can provide conservation leaders with a combination of funding, international recognition, professional development, communications support, and access to a wider conservation community.

1. £50,000 in Project Funding

Each winner receives £50,000 in project funding for one year.

This provides direct financial support for scaling up proven conservation work.

2. International Recognition

Whitley Award winners receive international recognition for their conservation leadership.

This increased visibility can help successful conservationists raise awareness of their projects and communicate their work to a broader audience.

3. Profile-Raising Opportunities

The award provides opportunities to raise the profile of both the conservation leader and their project.

For grassroots conservationists, increased visibility can be particularly valuable when building relationships with potential donors, partners, policymakers, conservation organisations, researchers, and other stakeholders.

4. Professional Communications and Media Support

Winners receive professional communications and media support.

This can help conservation leaders communicate the importance of their projects, share their results, and reach audiences beyond the communities in which they work.

5. Peer Learning

Whitley Award winners become part of a broader network of conservation leaders.

The programme provides opportunities for peer learning, enabling conservationists to exchange experiences, knowledge, and approaches with other leaders working on biodiversity and conservation challenges.

6. Training and Collaboration

Winners also gain access to training and collaboration opportunities.

These opportunities can help conservation leaders strengthen their professional capabilities and establish relationships with other people and organisations working to address environmental challenges.

7. Future Funding Opportunities

Winning a Whitley Award can also open the door to future opportunities.

Award winners become eligible for potential Continuation Funding and the Whitley Gold Award.

These opportunities can provide additional support for conservation leaders who continue to demonstrate strong impact.

A Global Community of Conservation Leaders

One of the most valuable aspects of the Whitley Awards is the community that comes with the award.

The Whitley Fund for Nature states that its growing global community includes more than 230 committed conservation leaders working across more than 80 countries.

These conservationists are working to address the biodiversity crisis through approaches rooted in:

  • Local knowledge;
  • Community engagement;
  • Practical conservation;
  • Science; and
  • Long-term commitment.

Being part of this network can provide conservation leaders with opportunities to exchange knowledge, build collaborations, and learn from peers working in different environmental and geographical contexts.

How to Apply for the Whitley Awards 2027

The application process consists of several key steps.

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility

Before beginning the application, prospective applicants should carefully review the Whitley Fund for Nature’s eligibility criteria.

Applicants should ensure that:

  • They meet the conservationist requirements.
  • They are nationals of the country in which they work.
  • Their project is community-based at the grassroots level.
  • Their conservation work is founded on science.
  • Their project has already demonstrated evidence of success.
  • They are seeking to scale up proven work.
  • Their project would benefit from additional funding and international support.

Applicants should also confirm that their specific type of conservation project falls within the activities supported by the Whitley Fund for Nature.

Step 2: Register on the Application Portal

Applicants must register for a WFN account through the online application portal.

Once registered, applicants receive login details that allow them to access and work on the application.

The application can be accessed and completed before the deadline.

Step 3: Complete the Online Application

After registering, applicants must complete the online application form.

Applicants should save their work regularly.

The application instructions specifically warn that information may be lost if the portal is closed without saving progress.

Step 4: Prepare the Logical Framework and Timeline

As part of the application process, applicants must download a Microsoft Word template from the portal for their logical framework and timeline.

The document should be completed and subsequently uploaded to the application portal.

Applicants should ensure they use the current year’s template because the application forms are updated annually.

Step 5: Prepare the Budget

Applicants must also download a Microsoft Excel template for their project budget.

The completed budget should then be uploaded through the application portal.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed budget is realistic, clearly explained, and connected to the activities and outcomes described in their application.

Step 6: Contact Three Referees

Applicants must nominate three referees to support their applications.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their referees submit their references before the application deadline.

This means candidates should contact their referees well in advance rather than waiting until the final days of the application period.

Applicants should also verify that their selected referees meet the eligibility requirements specified by the Whitley Fund for Nature.

Important Application Documents

Applicants should be prepared to work with several important application materials.

These include:

  • Online application form;
  • Logical framework and timeline;
  • Project budget;
  • Three referee references; and
  • Any other information requested through the official application portal.

The Whitley Fund for Nature specifically warns that applicants must use the current year’s templates.

Applications submitted using outdated forms from previous years will not be considered.

This makes it important for applicants to download the 2027 versions directly from the current application portal rather than relying on documents saved from previous application cycles.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline for the 2027 Whitley Awards

The official deadline is:

23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026

Applicants should ensure that the complete application process is finished before this deadline.

This includes allowing sufficient time for all three referees to submit their references.

Because referee submissions are the applicant’s responsibility, candidates should contact referees early and communicate the deadline clearly.

Visit HERE for more information about the Whitley Awards 2027.

When Will the Winners Be Announced?

The winners of the 2027 Whitley Awards will be announced during the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.

This ceremony provides an opportunity to celebrate the successful conservation leaders and their contributions to biodiversity conservation.

How to Make Your Application Competitive

Meeting the basic eligibility requirements is important, but conservation leaders should also think carefully about how they communicate their projects.

Clearly Define the Conservation Problem

Start by explaining the environmental or biodiversity challenge your project is addressing.

Explain:

  • What is happening?
  • Where is the problem occurring?
  • Which species, ecosystems, or communities are affected?
  • Why is the problem urgent?
  • What factors are driving the challenge?

A strong application should allow reviewers to quickly understand the importance of the conservation issue.

Demonstrate Evidence of Impact

Because the Whitley Awards support proven work, applicants should provide evidence that their approach is producing meaningful results.

Where appropriate, demonstrate:

  • Conservation outcomes;
  • Community outcomes;
  • Changes resulting from the intervention;
  • Monitoring results;
  • Data;
  • Field evidence;
  • Partnerships;
  • Lessons learned; and
  • Other measurable achievements.

Explain How the Project Will Scale

Applicants should clearly explain what additional funding will allow them to accomplish.

Do not simply state that more money is needed.

Explain specifically:

  • What activities will be expanded?
  • Which communities will benefit?
  • What additional conservation outcomes will be achieved?
  • What resources are required?
  • Why is this the right time to scale?
  • How will the £50,000 investment contribute to lasting impact?

Put Communities at the Centre

Since grassroots community involvement is a core requirement, applicants should demonstrate meaningful community engagement.

Explain how local people participate in decision-making, implementation, monitoring, conservation activities, or other relevant parts of the project.

Show the Scientific Foundation

Explain the scientific evidence or conservation knowledge underpinning the project.

The application should demonstrate that the proposed approach is not simply based on assumptions but is informed by appropriate evidence and knowledge.

Present a Realistic Budget

The budget should directly connect to the proposed project activities.

Applicants should be able to explain why each major expense is necessary and how the funding will contribute to the project’s conservation objectives.

Select Strong Referees

Because three referees are required, applicants should choose people who can provide meaningful evidence of their leadership, conservation experience, project achievements, and professional capabilities.

Most importantly, contact referees early enough to give them sufficient time to complete their references before the deadline.

Who Cannot Assume They Are Eligible?

Not every environmental project automatically qualifies for a Whitley Award.

For example, applicants should not assume eligibility solely because their work is described as:

  • Environmental;
  • Sustainable;
  • Green;
  • Climate-related; or
  • Nature-related.

The programme specifically requires eligible projects to involve grassroots communities and deliver practical conservation action founded on science.

The Whitley Fund for Nature also provides specific eligibility criteria explaining what it does and does not fund.

Therefore, applicants should carefully review the official eligibility guidance before submitting an application.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to be nominated?

No.

The application information explicitly states that applicants do not need to be invited or nominated to apply for a Whitley Award.

How much funding does each winner receive?

Each Whitley Award provides £50,000 in project funding over one year.

Is the £50,000 personal prize money?

The funding is described as project funding, meaning it is intended to support the successful conservation project.

Are the awards open internationally?

The Whitley Awards support conservation leaders internationally. The eligibility information states that winners are nationals of the country in which they are working.

Can early-career conservationists apply?

The programme describes its target applicants as dynamic, mid-career conservationists leading vital conservation projects.

Applicants should therefore carefully assess whether their professional experience and leadership level align with the programme’s expectations.

Does the project need community involvement?

Yes.

Eligible projects must involve communities at the grassroots level and deliver practical action founded on science.

Does the project need to be science-based?

Yes.

The programme specifically requires practical conservation action founded on science.

Do I need an invitation?

No.

Applicants can apply directly without an invitation or nomination.

How many referees are required?

Three referees are required.

When is the deadline?

Applications close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026.

When will winners be announced?

Winners will be announced during the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.

Official Application Resources

Prospective applicants should use the official Whitley Fund for Nature resources when preparing their applications.

  • Whitley Fund for Nature – Apply for a Whitley Award
  • Whitley Awards Eligibility Criteria
  • 2027 Whitley Awards Application Portal
  • Whitley Awards FAQs
  • Whitley Awards Application Guidelines

Conclusion

The 2027 Whitley Awards provide an important opportunity for established conservation leaders seeking to scale practical, science-based projects that are already delivering results at the grassroots level.

With £50,000 in project funding over one year, winners receive much more than financial support. The award also provides international recognition, communications and media support, peer learning, training, collaboration opportunities, and eligibility for future Continuation Funding and the Whitley Gold Award.

The programme’s emphasis on community participation, scientific foundations, proven conservation work, and lasting impact makes it particularly suited to conservation leaders who can demonstrate that their projects are already producing meaningful results and have a clear pathway for expansion.

The opportunity is also global in reach, with the Whitley Fund for Nature highlighting a community of more than 230 conservation leaders working across over 80 countries. This creates an international network through which conservationists can share knowledge, build collaborations, and contribute to broader efforts to address the biodiversity crisis.

For eligible mid-career conservationists, the 2027 Whitley Awards can provide both the financial resources and international platform needed to take a proven conservation initiative to the next stage.

The application deadline is 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026. Prospective applicants should begin early, carefully review the eligibility criteria, use the updated 2027 application templates, prepare a strong project budget and logical framework, and ensure that all three referees submit their references before the deadline.
