item.content:encoded:
Young Advocates for a Sustainable and Inclusive Future (YASIF) Nigeria is a youth-focused, nonprofit organization working to equip young people and women with practical digital, green, and employability skills that can help them respond to climate challenges, build sustainable livelihoods, and contribute to their communities.

Based in Abuja, Nigeria, YASIF combines youth empowerment, digital skills development, environmental sustainability, women’s empowerment, inclusion, entrepreneurship, and climate action. Through its programs and partnerships, the organization provides opportunities for young Nigerians to acquire relevant skills, access career development resources, participate in sustainability initiatives, and contribute to solutions addressing environmental and social challenges.

For young people looking for practical skills and opportunities connected to the digital economy, green economy, employment, entrepreneurship, and community development, YASIF offers several programs and initiatives worth exploring.

About YASIF Nigeria

Young Advocates for a Sustainable and Inclusive Future, commonly known as YASIF, is a Nigerian nongovernmental, nonprofit youth organization focused on creating sustainable solutions aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

The organization’s work is particularly connected to:

  • SDG 3: Good Health and Well-Being
  • SDG 4: Quality Education
  • SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production
  • SDG 13: Climate Action
  • SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals

YASIF’s approach is centered on the belief that young people and women can play a major role in addressing climate and sustainability challenges when they have access to appropriate skills, knowledge, networks, and opportunities.

The organization works to bridge the gap between skills development and practical community impact by combining digital education, employability training, environmental action, entrepreneurship, and grassroots initiatives.

YASIF’s Mission

YASIF’s mission is to equip young people and women with digital, green, and employability skills that can help transform climate challenges into opportunities for:

  • Income generation
  • Innovation
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Employment
  • Community development
  • Environmental sustainability

Rather than treating climate change solely as an environmental problem, YASIF’s programs seek to help young people identify ways to respond to environmental challenges while creating sustainable livelihoods.

YASIF’s Vision

The organization’s vision is a future in which young people and women lead climate solutions, build sustainable livelihoods, and thrive in a just and inclusive economy.

This vision places young people at the center of economic and environmental transformation.

It also recognizes the importance of ensuring that women and other groups that may experience barriers to opportunity are included in the transition toward a sustainable and digital economy.

Inclusion and Persons With Disabilities

Inclusion is an important component of YASIF’s work.

In alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals principle of “leave no one behind,” the organization collaborates with young people with disabilities (PWDs).

Through its programs and activities, YASIF seeks to create opportunities where young people from different backgrounds can participate, collaborate, develop skills, and contribute to community transformation.

This inclusive approach recognizes that young people should not be excluded from opportunities because of disability or other circumstances.

YASIF’s Impact

According to the information provided by the organization, YASIF has reported the following impact figures:

  • 23,000 youths engaged
  • 2,500 women impacted
  • 6 tons of plastic evacuated

These figures illustrate the organization’s focus on combining skills development with environmental and community-based action.

Its programs span digital skills, employability, women’s empowerment, plastic-waste management, sustainability, climate action, and youth leadership.

Free Digital Skills Opportunities Through YASIF

One of the major areas of YASIF’s current work is providing young people with access to digital skills development.

YASIF Nigeria has partnered with organizations including IAVE and IBM SkillsBuild to expand access to free digital skills training.

The program is intended for individuals looking for a credible and cost-free pathway to develop skills that are relevant to the modern workforce.

Participants can use such programs to strengthen their digital knowledge while exploring potential career and employment pathways.

The organization describes the program as providing access to in-demand digital skills and meaningful career opportunities.

What Participants Can Gain From the Digital Skills Program

The available program information highlights opportunities such as:

  • Free online learning
  • Digital skills development
  • Recognized certifications
  • Career-oriented learning
  • Access to mentorship
  • Networking opportunities
  • Potential internship opportunities
  • Exposure to skills relevant to the changing workforce

These components can be particularly valuable for young people who want to improve their employability without having to pay for expensive professional training.

Why Digital Skills Matter

The global employment landscape is changing rapidly as businesses, governments, nonprofits, and entrepreneurs increasingly depend on digital technologies.

Digital skills can help young people participate in:

  • Remote work
  • Digital entrepreneurship
  • Technology-related careers
  • Online freelancing
  • Business development
  • Digital marketing
  • Data-related roles
  • Technology-enabled social enterprises
  • Modern workplace environments

Free training initiatives can therefore provide an accessible starting point for individuals who want to build a foundation before pursuing more specialized education or employment.

Re-Skilling Revolution Africa Program

YASIF is also involved in the Re-Skilling Revolution Africa Program, which focuses on empowering Nigerian young people with digital skills.

The program is described as providing access to:

  • Free online courses
  • Certifications
  • Mentorship
  • Networking
  • Internship opportunities

The initiative is designed to help young Nigerians acquire skills that can support their participation in the digital economy and create pathways toward employment and professional development.

For individuals who may not have access to expensive training programs, free online learning combined with mentorship and networking can provide an important opportunity to begin developing marketable skills.

Empower Communities for Plastic Sustainability Project

Another major area of YASIF’s work is environmental sustainability, particularly plastic pollution.

The organization launched the Empower Communities for Plastic Sustainability (ECPS) project with support from the Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP).

The project focuses on promoting plastic sustainability within communities in:

  • Niger State
  • Kano State
  • Cross River State

The initiative aims to empower 1,000 women, young people, and persons with disabilities with digital and hands-on skills related to plastic waste management and sustainable practices.

What the ECPS Project Seeks to Achieve

The project is designed around several interconnected objectives:

  1. Increase awareness of plastic pollution.
  2. Equip communities with practical sustainability skills.
  3. Support women and young people.
  4. Include persons with disabilities in sustainability initiatives.
  5. Encourage entrepreneurship around plastic waste.
  6. Promote upcycling and circular-economy practices.
  7. Support grassroots environmental solutions.
  8. Strengthen local capacity for sustainable waste management.

The project demonstrates how environmental challenges can also become opportunities for skills development, entrepreneurship, innovation, and livelihood creation.

Plastic Waste as an Economic Opportunity

YASIF’s sustainability work goes beyond simply removing plastic waste from communities.

The organization promotes the idea that plastic waste can potentially become a resource when communities have the knowledge and skills needed to collect, process, reuse, and transform it into valuable products.

Through upcycling and circular-economy practices, participants can learn how waste materials may be converted into products that have economic or social value.

This approach connects environmental protection with livelihood development.

It can help communities address two challenges simultaneously:

  • Reducing environmental pollution
  • Creating opportunities for income and entrepreneurship

Project Waste-Free Communities

YASIF has also implemented the Project Waste-Free Communities initiative, which focuses on raising awareness and building the capacity of women and young people around waste management and environmental sustainability.

The organization has conducted activities in communities in Abuja, including:

  • Galadinmawa
  • Durunmi
  • Karonmagiji

Activities have included capacity-building sessions, awareness campaigns, upcycling training, and post-project evaluations.

Training for Women and Youth

One component of the initiative involved providing women and young people with practical training on upcycling.

The goal is to help participants understand how waste materials can be reused and transformed rather than simply discarded.

This type of training can contribute to:

  • Environmental awareness
  • Practical skills development
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Community participation
  • Sustainable consumption
  • Waste reduction

Climate Action and Youth Leadership

Climate action is another important part of YASIF’s activities.

The organization has participated in international climate-related activities, including a training session on local organizing and mobilization for climate justice at the Climate Justice Camp in Lebanon.

The event brought together organizers from approximately 30 countries.

Participation in international climate networks provides opportunities for Nigerian youth and organizations to exchange ideas and approaches with activists, organizers, and community leaders from other parts of the world.

It also reflects YASIF’s broader focus on connecting local community action with global sustainability and climate conversations.

Youth Leadership and the Sustainable Development Goals

YASIF also organizes activities aimed at strengthening youth leadership and engagement with the Sustainable Development Goals.

One featured event focuses on the theme:

Local Youth Action for SDGs and Beyond

The initiative highlights how young people can contribute to global development goals through practical action within their own communities.

The central message is that local initiatives can contribute to broader global change.

Youth participants can gain exposure to discussions around:

  • Sustainable development
  • Community action
  • Youth leadership
  • Climate solutions
  • Social impact
  • Local innovation
  • The Sustainable Development Goals

RRA SkillsBuild Pilot Project

YASIF has also documented the RRA SkillsBuild Pilot Project, highlighting its approach to empowering people through skills development.

The organization’s impact reporting provides an opportunity to understand how its programs are being implemented and how participants and communities are being affected.

Impact measurement is particularly important for development organizations because it helps demonstrate whether training and community interventions are translating into meaningful outcomes.

ECPS Idea Pitching and Award Ceremony

The Empower Communities for Plastic Sustainability (ECPS) project also featured an idea-pitching and award ceremony.

The event was held on 21 May 2025 at The Meeting Point Event Centre in Abuja.

The event provided a platform for participants and innovators to showcase ideas connected to plastic sustainability.

The ECPS initiative was developed with support from the Global Plastic Action Partnership and focused on empowering women, youth, and persons with disabilities to develop sustainable solutions to Nigeria’s plastic-waste challenge.

Idea-pitching activities can help participants develop skills in:

  • Problem identification
  • Innovation
  • Public presentation
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Sustainability
  • Project development
  • Community problem-solving

YASIF’s Three Major Strategic Objectives

The organization’s work can broadly be understood through three key objectives.

1. Digital and Employability Skills

YASIF aims to equip young people with practical digital and employability skills that prepare them for the modern workforce and the emerging green economy.

This includes initiatives involving:

  • Digital education
  • Online courses
  • Certifications
  • Mentorship
  • Networking
  • Career development
  • Internship opportunities

2. Women’s and Youth Empowerment Through Circular Economy

YASIF seeks to help women and young people transform plastic waste into valuable products through:

  • Upcycling
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Circular-economy practices
  • Practical skills training
  • Environmental education

This approach creates a connection between sustainability and economic empowerment.

3. Grassroots Climate and Environmental Solutions

The organization supports community-based solutions designed to:

  • Reduce plastic pollution
  • Strengthen local economies
  • Improve environmental awareness
  • Build climate resilience
  • Encourage community participation

The grassroots approach allows environmental initiatives to respond to challenges experienced directly by local communities.

Who Can Benefit From YASIF Opportunities?

YASIF’s programs are primarily relevant to young people and women, particularly those interested in:

  • Digital skills
  • Employability
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Green skills
  • Climate action
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Plastic waste management
  • Upcycling
  • Circular economy
  • Community development
  • Youth leadership

Some initiatives specifically include persons with disabilities, reflecting YASIF’s commitment to inclusive development.

However, eligibility varies from one YASIF program to another. Individuals should therefore review the requirements of the specific program before applying.

Why YASIF’s Programs Are Important

YASIF’s approach addresses several challenges facing young people and communities at the same time.

Young people need relevant skills to participate in an increasingly digital economy. At the same time, communities are dealing with climate change, plastic pollution, unemployment, and economic pressures.

By connecting skills development with sustainability, YASIF creates programs that address both economic and environmental needs.

For example, digital skills can improve employability, while green skills can prepare participants for opportunities in the emerging sustainable economy.

Similarly, plastic upcycling can simultaneously reduce waste and create opportunities for entrepreneurship.

Opportunities for Women

Women are a significant focus of YASIF’s work.

The organization seeks to provide women with opportunities to develop skills, participate in environmental initiatives, explore entrepreneurship, and contribute to community solutions.

Programs such as Project Waste-Free Communities and ECPS demonstrate how environmental sustainability can be used as a platform for women’s economic empowerment.

By learning practical skills around waste management, upcycling, and entrepreneurship, women can potentially develop new income-generating activities while contributing to cleaner communities.

Opportunities for Young People With Disabilities

YASIF’s commitment to inclusion extends to young people with disabilities.

The organization collaborates with young persons with disabilities as part of its effort to ensure that development opportunities are not restricted to people without disabilities.

This inclusive approach is particularly important in skills development because persons with disabilities can face barriers to education, employment, entrepreneurship, and participation in community programs.

YASIF’s model seeks to create spaces where young people can participate regardless of their status.

YASIF’s Geographic Focus

YASIF is based in Abuja, Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria, and many of its activities focus on Nigerian communities.

Its programs have included activities in locations such as:

  • Abuja
  • Niger State
  • Kano State
  • Cross River State

The organization’s international climate engagement also demonstrates connections beyond Nigeria, including participation in international climate activities.

Specific eligibility and geographic requirements vary by program.

How to Follow YASIF Opportunities

Young people and organizations interested in YASIF’s programs should monitor its official announcements for new applications, training cohorts, events, and community initiatives.

Because individual programs can have different eligibility requirements, application procedures, and closing dates, prospective participants should always read the specific announcement carefully before applying.

For programs involving digital skills, applicants should pay particular attention to:

  • Registration requirements
  • Age requirements, where applicable
  • Country or location requirements
  • Training duration
  • Certification details
  • Mentorship arrangements
  • Internship components
  • Application deadlines

YASIF Contact Information

Individuals who want to learn more about YASIF’s activities can contact the organization directly.

Organization: Young Advocates for a Sustainable and Inclusive Future (YASIF)

Location: Abuja, Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria

Phone: +234 701 869 9687

Email: info@yasif.org

For program-specific questions, prospective participants should contact YASIF using the organization’s official communication channels

Apply HERE today!

Is There a Deadline for the YASIF Opportunities?

The information provided does not state a specific deadline for the currently highlighted digital-skills opportunity.

The website indicates that applications for the next cohort are open, but no closing date is provided in the supplied information.

Therefore, interested applicants should apply as soon as possible and check the latest YASIF announcement for any subsequently published deadline.

To learn more about the Free Digital Skills Training in Nigeria, click HERE.

Conclusion

YASIF Nigeria provides a broad range of initiatives aimed at helping young people and women develop the skills, knowledge, and networks needed to participate in a changing economy while contributing to environmental and community solutions.

Its work spans digital skills, employability, green skills, women’s empowerment, youth leadership, plastic-waste management, upcycling, circular economy, climate action, and inclusion.

The organization’s digital-skills initiatives, including its work with partners such as IAVE and IBM SkillsBuild, provide young people with opportunities to pursue free online learning, certifications, mentorship, networking, and potential internship pathways.

At the same time, projects such as Empower Communities for Plastic Sustainability and Project Waste-Free Communities demonstrate how YASIF connects environmental action with practical skills, entrepreneurship, and community development.

With a particular focus on young people, women, and persons with disabilities, YASIF’s programs reflect an inclusive approach to sustainable development in Nigeria.

For young Nigerians seeking opportunities to improve their digital capabilities, develop employability skills, explore green careers, participate in environmental initiatives, or contribute to community development, YASIF is an organization worth monitoring for upcoming programs and application opportunities.

To explore and learn more about other training opportunities, visit the OFY page HERE.
